subject: OrchardPay discovery — POC qualification & agent/workflow requirements
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Gupta <maya@orchardpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: discovery call — OrchardPay needs for structured payouts and tool calls

Hi Maya — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Pain points you shared
- Current payout flow is brittle: multiple parsing steps to normalize merchant payout instructions (CSV → various internal formats).
- Many downstream systems require strongly-typed JSON (ledger entries, tax categories). Manual normalization is the biggest operational cost.
- Latency spikes during peak batch processing cause delayed settlements and customer tickets.
- Security: you need a path to meet PCI/sensitive-data requirements; sending raw PAN/account details to hosted third parties is a blocker.

Current stack (what you mentioned)
- In-house microservices (Go + K8s) that call a tokenized input normalization service.
- GPU-backed model infra for experiments (4x A100s) but no standardized inference orchestration.
- A payments ledger service that *requires* deterministic JSON payloads for downstream processing.

Success criteria for a POC
- Output: a deterministic, schema-validated JSON payload (fields and types enforced) for each payout instruction.
- Reliability: <100ms p50 inference for single-turn canonicalization, p95 under 350ms in our test environment.
- Cost target: material reduction vs current tokenized pipeline (we’ll discuss baseline metrics in follow ups).
- Security: option for Private/VPC or on-prem to avoid sending raw PII to a shared hosted endpoint.

Functional requirements we discussed
- Function/tool calling (model -> call payment-rails tooling) and a structured JSON handshake (schema-first).
- Controlled fallback strategy: explicit parse_error + confidence score if output deviates from schema.
- Auditability: per-request trace IDs and KV-cacheable prefixes for repeated merchants.

Attachments I’m sending here
- orchard_schema_example.json (very rough sketch of the JSON we’d expect)
- OP-MAP-v1.0.xlsx (a short mutual action plan template with owners/dates)

Next steps (proposed)
1) Your team to confirm the example schema and point out any mandatory fields we missed (due Thu 11/4).
2) We’ll draft a short POC plan (Redwood + OrchardPay private deployment option + acceptance tests) and share cost ballpark + timeline (by Mon 11/8).
3) Karthik to outline the runbook for function/tool calling integration and deterministic formatting options.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the first-draft POC plan once I have your schema feedback.

—
Evelyn Hart
Account Exec, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: orchard_schema_example.json (application/json), OP-MAP-v1.0.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Maya Gupta <maya@orchardpay.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: OrchardPay Eng Team <eng-team@orchardpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: discovery call — OrchardPay needs for structured payouts and tool calls

Evelyn — thanks for the clear recap, that captures the high level well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Mandatory fields: our ledger requires merchant_id, amount_cents, currency_iso, payout_method {type}, routing (masked on transit), tax_category. We’ll annotate the schema you sent and return by EOD Thu 11/4.
- Latency baseline: our current normalization service averages p50=220ms, p95=620ms in our staging runs. Your p95 target of 350ms would be a meaningful improvement.
- Security: for any PII (account numbers) we need a deployment option that keeps raw values inside our VPC. Sandbox with tokenized samples is fine for initial validation.
- Volume: daily peak ~120k instructions (batched overnight + sporadic real-time requests).

I’m attaching a small sample payload set and a short note from our infra lead on acceptable deployment patterns. We’re open to a Redwood Private or Dedicated model for the POC.

Timeline note: procurement wants an internal signoff by end of Q1 2027. If we get a POC plan + clear acceptance tests by Nov, we can move fast.

Thanks — I’ll send the annotated schema and payload samples on Thu.

—
Maya Gupta
Head of Product, OrchardPay
maya@orchardpay.com
Attachment stubs: orchard_sample_payloads.csv (text/csv), orchard_schema_annotations.json (application/json)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Maya Gupta <maya@orchardpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: discovery call — OrchardPay needs for structured payouts and tool calls

Hi all — quick technical thoughts to make the POC acceptance criteria concrete. I’ll iterate on this after I see the annotated schema from Maya.

Proposal highlights
1) Schema-first validation: Redwood will accept a JSON Schema (Draft-07 compatible) and enforce strict output shape during generation. If model output deviates, we produce a structured error object that includes a parse_error enum, confidence score, and the raw output for auditing.
2) Deterministic formatting approach:
   - Use function-calling mode with explicit parameter types + required fields.
   - Add a post-generation verification step (schema validator) before the response is returned to the caller; any deviation triggers deterministic repair attempts (up to N retries) with an operation log.
3) Tool/function calling:
   - Define lightweight tool signatures for downstream calls (e.g., call_create_payout(payout_json: object) -> {status, id, errors}).
   - We recommend decoupling: Redwood returns vetted payout_json; a separate idempotent service performs the final ledger write.
4) Performance knobs for POC:
   - Quantization profile recommendation (int8/llm-int8) for cost/latency tradeoffs.
   - Sticky KV prefixes for merchant templates to reduce warm-start token costs.

Acceptance test checklist (draft)
- 50 deterministic test prompts provided by OrchardPay that map to edge cases (malformed memo, weird currency codes, missing routing).
- For each prompt: generated payout_json must validate against the agreed schema; parse_error should be empty for >= 95% of prompts.
- Latency: p50 <= 180ms in our POC staging harness, p95 <= 350ms.
- Security: POC must run in your VPC or a Private deployment with KMS integration for secret material.

I’ve attached a short playbook that explains our function-calling + repair loop and a sample validator harness we can run together.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment stubs: redwood_toolcall_playbook.pdf (application/pdf), validator_harness_instructions.md (text/markdown)

Maya — thanks, and I appreciate the quick turnaround on the annotated schema when you have it. Finalizing owners/timeline here so we’re all clear: 

Action items
- Maya / OrchardPay: return annotated schema + 50 representative test prompts + sample payload set by Thu 11/4 (owner: Maya).
- Redwood (Evelyn): deliver POC plan + rough pricing + proposed infra option (Private vs Dedicated) by Mon 11/8 (owner: Evelyn).
- Redwood (Karthik): deliver validator harness + playbook + recommended quantization profile by Mon 11/8 (owner: Karthik).
- Joint: Schedule a 60m POC kickoff (tech sync) for week of 11/15 — propose Tue 11/16 10am PT; please confirm availability.

Acceptance criteria (short)
- Deterministic JSON payloads that validate against the agreed schema for >=95% of curated prompts.
- POC latency in staging meets p95 <= 350ms and p50 <= 180ms.
- POC demonstrates a deployment pattern that meets OrchardPay’s security requirement (VPC/KMS).

I’ve attached the mutual action plan (OP-MAP-v1.0.xlsx) for owners/dates and included links to the HubSpot deal and our shared Drive folder above. If the annotated schema looks like a go, we’ll slot resources for an accelerated POC.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

—
Evelyn Hart
